new: "cognate of", "related to", "compare X", "akin to X", any of these followed by "a variation of", "a derivative of", "a prolonged form of" or "a form of", a word joined by "and" or "or" to a word already marked a root, and a word or number in parentheses right after such a word) is a root. A root that stands in none of the cited verses does not refuse the tag; the tag's other words decide it. So a lexicon line quoted whole ("from σύν and ἔρχομαι", "a primary word (compare ἄνθρωπος)", "from a variation of γένος", "probably akin to χράομαι") does not refuse a tag whose own word or number stands in the cited verse. The join by "and" or "or" applies only when the word before it is already a root, so two claimed words or numbers joined by "and" are both still checked; a tag whose only word is an absent "compare X" is still refused (ASK 653; Shared Library, the one copy). The "compare", "akin to" and joined-word forms are not shown by a run.
